lede: Bill owns both sidelines in Tampa at Dallas tonight — his first free point of the season, and he has needed one. Then Sunday hands us Mark against Brian twice in the same afternoon.

beats.text: Buccaneers at Cowboys, 8:15, and he owns both benches. Tampa is 0-4 with Jalon Daniels filling in for Baker Mayfield's dislocated thumb and Dallas is laying a touchdown and a half, so the football should be one-sided — but the point lands either way. On seven, six behind Mark, he'll take it however it comes.

The 49ers go to Seattle at 4:25 and the Ravens go to Atlanta on Sunday night. Mark owns San Francisco and Baltimore; Brian owns Seattle and Atlanta. First place against joint second, two head-to-heads in one afternoon, and every point that changes hands moves directly between them. Nothing else this week comes close.

beats.tag: Jon and Patrick, level on nine
beats.text: Indianapolis at Pittsburgh is the other direct collision. Patrick's Colts have won two straight behind Jonathan Taylor; Jon's Steelers are 2-2 and lost in Cleveland to a 56-yarder. Pittsburgh favored by a field goal at home, and one of them walks out of Sunday clear of the other.

Houston at Tennessee: Harrison's 0-4 Texans against Jon's 0-4 Titans, and somebody finally has to win a game. The Texans are favored by a touchdown on the road, which is the market's verdict on Tennessee's 37 points in four weeks. Second-lowest total on the board.
